summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update3.json → valid=true; first attempt was rejected for using conclusion 'holds' without a fixed experiment, corrected to 'explained'). Two records, source-only since this run's experiment capacity is exhausted. (1) Verification of the weakest link behind the two earlier A2 findings: after the known-leader veto is skipped for a LeadershipTransfer-marked RequestVote, the receiver still applies, in order, the same-term duplicate-vote rule (raft.go:1697-1705, grants only for the identical candidate), the log up-to-dateness rules (1707-1723), then persists and grants (1725-1732) — so a fresh-term, caught-up voting candidate is granted and can win, while a non-voting target fails the earlier suffrage veto and can only cost the leader; runCandidate's tally (363-385) confirms one granted voter suffices in a 3-voter cluster. Producer uniqueness is recorded as a Fact: candidateFromLeadershipTransfer is stored true only in timeoutNow (2209-2214) and reset on every runCandidate exit, so the vote-bypass privilege rides on exactly one candidacy after a TimeoutNow. Competing explanations are preserved as counterevidence (a same-term vote already persisted for a rival, persist failure, or a strictly longer voter log each deny the vote), which narrows the claim rather than refuting it. (2) A new paused lead with a concrete discriminator: the mixed-version pre-vote fallback treats a peer error containing "unexpected command" as a granted pre-vote (raft.go:2082-2088), yet that constant is this version's processRPC default text (raft.go:21-24) while an unknown RPC type fails earlier in NetworkTransport.handleCommand with "unknown rpc type %d" (net_transport.go:716-717) — if the counterpart version reports that text (or a transport-level failure), the fallback never fires and a candidate whose only reachable peers are pre-vote-incapable gets refused, contrary to the stated rolling-upgrade intent. It is deliberately paused, not asserted, because the counterpart version's code is outside the authorized snapshot; resume conditions are recorded explicitly.
